Adaptively densify lines for a projection

Source: R/densify.R
densify.Rd

Insert vertices along great circle arcs exactly where a target projection bends them, so that straight chords drawn between output vertices stay within tolerance of the true projected curve. This is the adaptive resampling scheme of d3-geo (Bostock), generalized to paths and to segment meshes.

densify(
  x,
  target,
  source = "OGC:CRS84",
  tolerance = NULL,
  pixels = 2048L,
  max_depth = 16L
)

Arguments

x

a two-column matrix of lon,lat (a path), a list of such matrices, a segment mesh (a list with vb, a 4 x n vertex matrix with rows x, y, z, h, and is, a 2 x m segment index matrix, 1-based, as used by rgl's mesh3d), or a wkpool vertex-pool topology from the wkpool package (any wk-handleable geometry via wkpool::establish_topology()); pools carrying z or m vertex values are refused, as densification cannot invent them at new vertices

target

projection for which to densify (proj string, WKT, authority code - anything PROJ accepts)

source

coordinate system of the input, default 'OGC:CRS84' (longitude, latitude); authority codes are axis-normalized so 'EPSG:4326' input is still given as lon,lat

tolerance

maximum allowed deviation, in units of target (usually metres); if NULL (the default) it is derived from the projected extent of the input as min(diff(range))/pixels

pixels

notional output width/height used to derive the default tolerance, i.e. "keep error under about one part in pixels of the plot"; ignored when tolerance is supplied

max_depth

maximum bisection depth per input segment (each level at most doubles the vertex count of a segment)

Value

the same kind of object as x, with vertices added: a matrix for a path, a list of matrices for a list, a mesh with appended vertices and refined is for a mesh, a wkpool with appended vertices (freshly minted .vx ids), refined directed segments, and .feature provenance carried onto every refined segment

Details

The error metric is evaluated in the plane of the target projection: the great circle midpoint of each candidate segment is forward-projected and compared to the segment's planar chord (perpendicular distance, plus a parametric check that catches strong shear). Segments are split recursively until they pass or max_depth is reached. No inverse transforms are used and each point is projected exactly once.

Coordinates are returned in the coordinates of source (geographic by default): project the result yourself for plotting, e.g. with rproj_xy() or your tool of choice.

Points that cannot be projected (for example beyond the horizon of an orthographic projection) do not error: segments touching them are left un-densified, and refinement stops at unprojectable midpoints. Clipping is out of scope here.

References

https://bost.ocks.org/mike/example/

Examples

s <- segment(c(140, -164), c(-89, 80))
d <- densify(s, "+proj=laea +lon_0=147 +lat_0=-42")
nrow(d)
#> [1] 95
plot(rproj_xy(d, "+proj=laea +lon_0=147 +lat_0=-42"), type = "l", asp = 1)
